name: Noir
typeSystem: Static and strong, with Rust-inspired syntax specialised for zero-knowledge programs. Constrained code requires statically bounded control flow, while current Noir also has dynamically sized vectors and permits runtime-bounded loops in unconstrained Brillig code.
runtime: Noir compiles constrained computation to ACIR and unconstrained witness-generation code to Brillig bytecode. A proving backend such as Barretenberg executes the workflow and produces or verifies a zero-knowledge proof.

runtimes.name: ACVM + proving backend
runtimes.role: ACVM evaluates ACIR constraints and coordinates a proving backend such as Barretenberg; unconstrained witness-generation code is executed separately as Brillig bytecode.

runtimes.name: Brillig VM
runtimes.role: Executes unconstrained Noir code used during witness generation, whose relevant results must be constrained by the circuit.

compilers.name: nargo
compilers.role: Noir's build tool and compiler, compiling source to ACIR and orchestrating proof generation/verification.

concurrencyModel: N/A (circuit-based; describes a single deterministic computation to be proved, not a concurrent process).
